To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of lead oxide to cement mortars decreases the mechanical strength and that the release of lead depends on the initial concentration and the time of leach.
the release of PbO from stabilized/solidified mortars depends on the initial concentration and the duration of the leaching test.
the release of lead during the TCLP test and the effectiveness of Solidification/Stabili zation process depend on the initial concentration and the leaching time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of the release of the pollutant PbO from mortars.
the development of a new technology for the treatment of hazardous waste PbO, which is an important step in the management of hazardous waste.
a new approach to the modeling of the performance of the process of Stabilization/Solidification of hazardous compound.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the process of Solidified/Stabilization of lead is effective, and that the use of cement CEM II- 42.5 as hydraulic binder for the treatment of leaded waste can be recommended.
the stabilization/solidification process of lead oxide by cement is effective and can be considered as a viable option for the treatment of lead oxide contaminated soil.
the process of stabilization/solidification of PbO by cement is a viable option for PbO contaminated materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the stabilization/solidification process is an efficient and effective method to treat lead contaminated soil.
the use of cement as a solidifying/stabilizing agent for the PbO is a promising technique.
the process of Solidified / Stabilization is effective in reducing the mobility of PbO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cement is a good way to stabilize Pb.
the release of lead during the TCLP test is much lower than the limit of 5 mg/L.
the release of the lead is controlled by the surface area of the samples and that it is not possible to predict the release rate of Pb from the samples by using a simple diffusion model.
